Use microsoft word with autosave on instead.

body:
Notes has this one bug where if you handwrite a very long note, the handwriting becomes very laggy and the iPad gets very hot (also drains battery really quickly.) If you continue writing, it will eventually crash and your handwriting doesn’t save starting from where it started lagging.

The solution? Let us users choose to break out their handwritten notes into multiple pages. It would stop the lag and battery drain, as well as providing additional benefits like being able to export or print notes without the handwriting being cut off, as well as being organized with our notes. I’m looking to switch away from Goodnotes and I’m in love with Apple Notes’ aesthetic and the PencilKit tools, but this issue is the only thing that is preventing me from switching to it full-time.

title: Begrudgingly to enthusiastically
body:
I was surprised Apple of all companies would prompt me to rate their on their App Store but there we are. 

That said, having been a HEAVY digital notes user on mobile since the Apple Newton MessagePad 2000 (I was one of those guys with the keyboard), Im here to say Apple
Notes has become a necessity for me, in all the best ways.

I was a heavy Evernote user until I began dipping my toes back into the Apple Notes pool. Slowly at first, and the all at once, I had seamlessly migrated all of my rich media notes over and began to work on the areas where feature gaps hampered my flow of data collection and organization. Those gaps have closed up beautifully in the last few major OS upgrades.

The one caveat I’ll mention is that you need to upgrade your OS to access some features…which is a poor choice on Apple’s part, but as my life is organized by files, folders, and notes, I feel Apple has built a Trinity of features I’m very comfortable with.

title: Powerful notes app! Hardly!
body:
I started using Notes with my iPhone 5. It was so rudimentary I gave up on it within two months. I adopted Evernotes and never looked back. It’s a super powerful notes and tasks app that keeps getting better.

Last year Evernotes began inundating me with advertising by email and push notifications. They want me to upgrade. For me, there is no value in paying even the 40% discounted ($100/yr) subscription as I would never use the added features.

I’m looking for a replacement.

I downloaded and tried Apple Notes again. I cannot believe that after 10 years there are few changes. While the rest of the world has learned to ride the app “cycles”,  Notes is still on training wheels!

It does not support custom tags to a note. It’s impossible to create a note inside a custom folder and difficult at best to move a note to a custom folder. There is no way to copy a note to a new note and rename it. I have a tasks format that works well for me; I copy this week’s task list to a new list, rename it then remove items from the previous week that were accomplished. This leaves me with carry overs to the new week of tasks without having to edit manually and also gives me an archive of the previous week’s tasks from the original note for review if needed.

These are just a few basic things that Apple Notes cannot do.

When will Apple realize that this is the 21st century and create apps that match their cutting edge world class hardware and operating systems? Hey Apple - It’s not 1990! Get with the times!

Apple Notes: Powerful app? Hardly.

title: Works Well But a Few Suggestions
body: I have recently been exploring Apple Notes more since I will be graduating from school soon and will no longer have access to OneNote without paying for it. I have discovered that I do enjoy all of the features provided by this app, but I have some suggestions on how Apple could make it even better. Firstly would be to add the ability to place a highlight colour over text. This way, more college and university students would be more likely to use it because they could effectively integrate both typing and handwriting together like they do in OneNote. Secondly, I would recommend including the ability for a page to continue expanding sideways rather than only downward. This would help for those who have larger writing but wish to continue their sentence on the same line for example because they could just continue writing and know that the page would expand more sideways. Thirdly, I would recommend including the ability to convert writing into typed text as som other applications do. This way for people who have a difficult time reading their writing when they come back to it, they could convert it into typed text and know for certain what they had written. Lastly - I would recommend more integration of text and typing like OneNote has, like the ability to draw on top of text rather than having to write below the text. This could include things such as the ability to draw a circle around a typed word for example. Overall, Apple did a great job when developing this app and I will definitely be continuing to use it in the future. Thank you Apple!
